Global Warming Unleashes its Fury on the Land Down Under

Numerous communities in eastern Australia were devastated by massive flooding in the early hours of January 10th. In one small town, panicked citizens were forced to evacuate to their rooftops by a tsunami-like flash flood.

If the local emergency response teams had not been prepared with lifeboats and helicopters, there would have been a significant loss of life. The cost and magnitude are still unclear, though experts suggest that there has been significant damage to major infrastructure. Scientists fear that the Great Barrier Reef could also be in danger of receiving the runoff from the floods. They have suggested to the government that they should start redirecting polluted water away from this sensitive area. The floods were caused by the hot ocean water off the coast of Australia.

As water temperatures continued to rise, the atmosphere was filled with water vapor. If there is too much water vapor, there is increased chance of weather-related natural disasters and violent storms.

Shouldn't we, as a global society feel compelled to do more to combat global warming? With the support of citizens, leaders could enact laws that would protect future generations. If we all work together, we will create change.

Now, it's your turn to write a short news article about an event in your area. Were there any witnesses? What did they recount?

Instructions:
Imagine you are a reporter for your local newspaper. There has been a terrible storm that has caused damage in your area. Your boss asks you to write an article about it.
Write a 100-150 word news article. (2/3 paragraphs)

In your first two sentences, focus on the important information (who, what, when, where, why).
Then, give the reader the details.

Use simple, compound and complex sentences.

It's time to review your news article.

When you are writing a news article, remember to:
  • Include the key information at the beginning of the article.
  • Provide additional information.
  • Include sentences that suggest cause and effect.
  • Add a quote if there was a witness to the event.
  • Include the Simple Past Passive.
Proofread your news article for any spelling, grammar or punctuation errors.

Writing a News Article - Simple Past Passive
When you are writing a news article or giving an interview, you can include the Simple Past Passive to describe something done by someone at sometime in the past.
Object + was / were + past participle

Example:
The weather was affected by the unexpected cold currents.
Was / Were + Object + past participle?

Example:
Was the weather affected by the cold currents?
Numerous communities in Eastern Australia were devastated by massive flooding.
The hot ocean water off the coast of Australia was blamed for the floods.
Writing a News Article - If Clauses
When you are writing a news article, you can also include conditionals to describe cause and effect as well as hypothetical situations.
There are different types of conditional sentences.

to devastate
to destroy much or most of (something); to cause great damage or harm to (something)
(verb)
Example: The violent weather devastated the community.
engenn7le17ob08aud01
These are words you would read in a news article about weather and the environment.
tsunami
a very high, large wave in the ocean usually caused by an earthquake under the ocean
(noun)
Example: The tsunami caused widespread devastation.
engenn7le17ob08aud02
flash flood
a sudden, large amount of water covering an area of land that is usually dry
(noun)
Example: The flash flood caught citizens by surprise.
engenn7le17ob08aud03
infrastructure
the basic equipment and structures such as roads and bridges that are needed for a country, region
(noun)
Example: The wild weather affected a lot of major infrastructure in the city.
engenn7le17ob08aud05
drought
a long period of time during which there is very little or no rain
(noun)
Example: Australia has suffered many periods of drought.
engenn7le17ob08aud06
to enact
to make a bill officially become part of the law
(verb)
Example: Leaders could enact laws that would protect future generations.
engenn7le17ob08aud07
run-off
water that drains from the land to waterways
(noun)
Example: The polluted run-off could damage the Great Barrier Reef.
engenn7le17ob08aud08
vapor
a substance that is in the form of a gas or that consists of very small drops or particles mixed with the air
(noun)
Example: As water temperatures continued to rise, the atmosphere was filled with water vapor.
engenn7le17ob08aud09
to compel
to make something happen; to force something
(verb)
Example: Hopefully, country leaders will feel compelled to act.
engenn7le17ob08aud04
atmosphere
the whole mass of air that surrounds the Earth
(noun)
Example: The atmosphere is made up of gases.
